assessment: This manuscript describes an elegant chemical-genetic strategy to discover that human oxidoreductase HSD17B11 is a major contributor to the bioactivation of the dialkinylcarbinol class of cytotoxic natural products. Mechanistic work further revealed that the reactive metabolites generated by HSD17B11 modify lysine and cysteine side-chains on proteins, leading to an unfolded protein response and apoptotic cell death. This study thus provides a plausible mechanism to explain how dialkynylcarbinol compounds exert their cytotoxic properties and identifies enzyme targets for controlling this process in human cells.
